findings.summary: The new `rootGitignore` test-task input and its `Measured:` comment are justified entirely by `FreshCheckoutTest asserts check-gate-scope refuses when .gitignore stops ignoring .tmp/` -- a test that is not in this commit (it went out with the M0.31 revert). No remaining test in the tree reads the root .gitignore; grep confirms the only other references are prose. Residue of the reverted half.
findings.failure_scenario: Over-declaring an input can only cause extra reruns, so there is no false green here. The cost is a comment that names a nonexistent test as its evidence: the next reader either deletes the input as unused -- and M0.31's test then goes UP-TO-DATE across exactly the .gitignore edit it exists to catch, the defect the comment describes -- or trusts a `Measured:` claim that cannot be reproduced against this tree.

findings.summary: The fixture's post-tar sanity assertion pins `scripts/check-gate-scope.sh`, and line 69 asserts `.tmp/` is absent. Neither is needed by the one remaining test, whose subject is scripts/check-harness-tests.sh and whose only load-bearing fixture invariant is line 70 (`.harness` absent). The tracked-list equality at 66 already subsumes the existence check, more strongly.
findings.failure_scenario: M0.31 edits check-gate-scope.sh and may rename or split it; the moment it moves, this unrelated test goes red reporting `sanity: the tar copy must have produced the tree` -- a false RED in the class written to eliminate false REDs. Pinning scripts/check-harness-tests.sh instead would make the sanity check fail only for a reason the test is about.

findings.summary: `import java.io.IOException` is unused -- no method in the file declares or catches it; every helper throws Exception. Left behind by the four removed tests.
findings.failure_scenario: No behavioural risk. It is the cheapest available signal that the file was narrowed rather than rewritten, and it survives because no gate in scripts/ checks unused imports.

findings.summary: gate() sets HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME to exactly the values scrub(pb, dir) already set two lines earlier, under a comment justifying them by `the personal ignore file, which decides check-gate-scope's answer`. The rationale belongs to a removed test; the assignment is a no-op duplicate.
findings.failure_scenario: Harmless today. It becomes harmful the moment scrub()'s HOME handling is changed for a reason: the duplicate silently overrides it for gate() only, and the divergence is invisible because both sites currently agree.

findings.summary: The gate is only ever exercised at GATE_SCOPE=full. The staged production line is unconditional and at top level, so the direct mutations all die -- but the delta path, which is the mode pre-commit actually runs, reaches the same redirect and is unconstrained.
findings.failure_scenario: Surviving mutation: replace `mkdir -p .harness` (scripts/check-harness-tests.sh:37) with `[ "$GATE_SCOPE" = "full" ] && mkdir -p .harness`. This test stays green because gate() pins full scope. In a fresh checkout at the default delta scope with any scripts/*.sh or buildSrc/* file staged -- the ordinary pre-commit case -- `relevant` is non-empty, control falls through to the redirect with .harness absent, and the original false RED is reproduced exactly. M0.24 already owns the delta pathspec of this script, so that is where a delta-mode fresh-checkout case belongs rather than widening M0.29.

findings.summary: testing.md rule 17 says scratch goes under build/tmp, never the system temp directory. `@TempDir` resolves to java.io.tmpdir; buildSrc/build.gradle.kts sets no `systemProperty("java.io.tmpdir", ...)` and there is no junit-platform.properties. Pre-existing convention -- ModuleGateTest does the same -- so this is a consistency note, not a defect introduced alone.
findings.failure_scenario: This fixture tars the entire tracked tree per test, so unlike ModuleGateTest's smaller fixtures it puts the whole repository into the system temp directory on every run. On a constrained tmpfs that is a failure mode outside Gradle's clean path, and it is the case rule 17 exists for.
